proposed.explanation:
ETEL's FY2025 results show strong fundamental growth that supports continuing to hold your 300 shares over your 5–7-year horizon. Revenue grew roughly 31% year-on-year (from 81.68 bn to 106.67 bn EGP), net profit more than doubled (from 10.11 bn to 22.58 bn EGP), and EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP per share. At the current price of 141.95 EGP, the implied P/E is about 11.9×, which is reasonable for a company growing at this pace. Total equity expanded 39% to 63.69 bn EGP, indicating the profit growth is being retained and building the balance sheet.

Risks to keep in mind: (1) The balance sheet is leveraged – total assets of 225.88 bn EGP against equity of 63.69 bn EGP implies liabilities of roughly 162.19 bn EGP (debt-to-equity ≈ 2.5×), so a downturn could pressure earnings. (2) You only have one year of comparative data; a single strong year does not guarantee a sustained trend. (3) ETEL already represents about 68% of your 62,585 EGP portfolio, which is concentrated for a medium-risk investor saving for a child's education. I cannot recommend buying more ETEL because the diversification cap (no single company > 50% of portfolio) is already breached, and I have no evidence on alternative Egyptian-listed names to diversify into. (4) No dividend information is provided, so income contribution is unknown.

Given the strong growth, reasonable valuation, and your 5–7-year time frame, holding the existing 300 shares is the most balanced action. I would not sell, as the fundamentals are positive and the horizon suits a growth position. I would not buy more, due to the concentration limit and the single-year data set. Consider reviewing the position again when FY2026 results are available to confirm the growth trend is sustainable, and look for opportunities to diversify into a second or third holding once you have evidence on other candidates.
